title: A Nahuatl-derived account has Motecuhzoma identify himself to Cortes
summary: A Nahuatl-tradition account has Motecuhzoma answer Cortes that he is the king, and welcome him.
body: Fordham's Aztec accounts, drawn from the Nahuatl tradition, have Cortes ask whether the speaker is Motecuhzoma and have the king say yes, then rise to welcome him. This is a later Indigenous narrative of the meeting, not Cortes's own letter and not a transcript from 1519. The wording on the page includes: "Cortés When Motecuhzoma [Montezuma] had given necklaces to each one, Cortés asked him: "Are you Motecuhzoma? Are you the king? Is it true that you are the king Motecuhzoma?" And the king said: "Yes, I am Motecuhzoma." Then he stood up to welcome Cortés; he came forward, bowed his head low and addressed him in these words: "Our lord, you are weary. The journey has". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
